To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
adiabatics is a promising approach for ultraconstrained pervasive devices.
adiabatice 2N-21P and SAL logic countermeasures seem to be the most promising candidates for ultraconstrained pervasive devices.
adiabatically operated 2N- 2N2P or SAL circuits are suitable countermeasures against DPA attacks for ultraconstrained RFID-tags.
In summary, our research is concerned with
lightweight cryptography and DPA countermeasures.
the development of lightweight cryptographic algorithms that are secure against physical attacks and the implementation of these algorithms on pervasive computing devices.
the question of how to make ubiquitous computing safe.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
adiabatics is the only way to go.
SAL seems to be the most promising candidate for DPA countermeasure in ultraconstrained devices.
SAL and 2N- 2N2P are the only countermeasures that are both effective against DPA attacks and suitable for ultraconstrained pervasive devices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have found that there are no countermeasures which are both effective against side channel attacks and at the same time cheap enough to be implemented in ultraconstrained devices such as passive RFID tags.
adiabatically powered SAL seems to be the most promising approach to achieve DPA resistance in ultraconstrained devices.
the security and performance of a cryptographic system are strongly coupled and that a trade-off between security and performance is necessary.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the security and cost requirements of pervasive computing devices have to be considered together, and that a trade-off between both is often necessary.
the field of lightweight cryptography and DPA countermeasures is still very young and has to be further developed in order to meet the needs of the Ubiquitous Computing era.

a careful analysis of the tradeoff between the security of a pervasive device and its energy consumption is required, because a security increase might come at the price of a higher power consumption.
